idea-plugin.name: Bracket Colorizer
idea-plugin.description:
Colorizes matching brackets by nesting depth ("rainbow brackets"): every pair of (), [], {} (and optionally <>) gets the color of its nesting level, so brackets that sit inside each other are easy to tell apart.

Uses each language's syntax highlighter to avoid recognized comments, strings, regular expression literals, and markup text. Files without a working syntax highlighter are left unchanged.

Plain text and Markdown files are skipped, so that ordinary link syntax such as [text](url) stays calm. Code fenced inside a Markdown file is still colorized.

The colors are fully configurable, either in the Bracket Colorizer tool window on the right hand side of the IDE (applied live) or under Settings | Editor | Bracket Colorizer: pick a color per nesting level, add or remove levels, and optionally mark unmatched brackets.

Instead of hand picked colors you can also pick a ready made palette under From template: the bracket colors of VS Code Dark+, VS Code Light+, VS Code High Contrast Dark, One Dark Pro, Dracula, Nord, or the Viasfora rainbow. Your own colors can be saved as a named template as well. A template also carries the bracket types, the repeat, bold and unmatched switches, which it ticks in the form when it is selected and which stay editable afterwards. Change template edits the one that is selected, and Customize templates manages the list: remove entries, clear it completely, or put the built in templates back without losing the ones you saved.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.2.0

Nesting colors no longer have to be picked one at a time. Next to the hand picked colors there is now a second way to dress up your brackets: templates. Seven of them ship with the plugin, each holding the bracket colors of a color scheme you probably know already, namely VS Code Dark+, VS Code Light+, VS Code High Contrast Dark, One Dark Pro, Dracula, Nord, and the Viasfora rainbow. Pick one from the dropdown and the whole form follows along: the level colors, the color for unmatched brackets, which bracket types are colorized, and the repeat, bold and unmatched switches. Nothing is locked afterwards, so a template is a starting point rather than a cage.

Your own palettes belong in that list just as much. Save as template turns the colors you picked by hand into a named entry of your own. Change template opens any template, including the ones that ship with the plugin, so its name, its colors, its number of levels and its switches can be reworked, then kept with Save or thrown away with Discard. Customize templates keeps the list itself in order: change or remove single entries, clear the whole list, or put the built in templates back the way they shipped. Restoring them never touches the templates you saved yourself.

Your hand picked colors stay exactly where they are while a template is in use, so switching back to them is always a single click.

1.0.0

Initial public release with configurable nesting colors, live tool window settings, unmatched bracket highlighting, and optional angle bracket support.
